blocks.html: Field Sales is a sales approach in which representatives meet prospects or customers in person, typically at their offices or business locations, to present solutions, build relationships, and close deals.

Field Sales is commonly used in B2B and enterprise environments where personal interaction plays an important role in winning business. Unlike inside sales, which relies on phone calls and digital communication, field sales focuses on face-to-face engagement to better understand customer needs, build trust, and manage complex buying decisions.
Field sales professionals usually follow a structured process that includes:

items.html: Scheduling in-person meetings or site visits
Presenting products or services directly to decision-makers
Closing deals and maintaining ongoing client relationships

blocks.html: Builds stronger customer relationships through personal interaction
Improves trust and credibility with prospects
Enables on-site demonstrations and tailored presentations
Supports complex or high-value sales cycles
Increases opportunities for upselling and long-term partnerships
A software company sends a sales representative to a manufacturing client’s office to demonstrate its automation platform, discuss operational challenges, and finalize a multi-year contract.

Field Sales remains an effective strategy for businesses selling complex, customized, or high-value solutions. By combining personal engagement with consultative selling, it helps organizations strengthen relationships and close larger deals.
